title: Audit Exception Pack
learningObjective: Use shaping decisions to keep current policy stronger than stale shortcuts and to make missing exception facts impossible to miss.
chapterConcept: Precedence, stale-context control, and missing-information handling
lifecycleCue: This pack assumes Discovery and Selection are already complete. The run focuses on Shaping, then review and iteration.
caseBrief: A finance coordinator wants a reusable envelope for a travel-meal exception review. The package must separate current policy from old shortcut notes, make missing facts obvious, and produce a route-ready recommendation without silently approving the exception.
successCriteria: Keep instructions, evidence, dynamic facts, and checks visibly distinct.
Make precedence and missing-information handling explicit instead of implied.
Use a reviewable output contract that another reviewer could inspect quickly.
Make the package reliable enough to hand off without hidden assumptions.
outputReminder: Did the response follow the current source of record instead of weaker notes?
Did it keep the required format rather than collapsing into a generic paragraph?
Did it state uncertainty or escalation when facts were missing?

precedenceRules.label: Current finance policy outranks old team shortcuts and verbal memory.
Most recent note in the package wins, even if it is informal.
Leave precedence unstated and let the model infer it.

handlingOptions.label: State what is missing and route only after the required details are captured.
Ask for the missing details before giving the routing answer.
Infer the likely approval path from the available facts.

blocks.label: Travel Audit Analyst
blocks.text: Act as a careful travel audit analyst. Explain the rule clearly, stay inside approved policy, and avoid inventing approvals or exceptions.

blocks.label: Approved Finance Sources Only
blocks.text: Use only the approved travel policy excerpt and the current exception procedure in REFERENCE. Do not rely on memory or informal team shortcuts.

blocks.label: Do Not Auto-Approve
blocks.text: Do not approve the exception yourself. State whether the request appears policy-compliant and identify the required next step.

blocks.label: Meals Cap Policy
blocks.text: Approved finance policy (2026): same-day travel meals above $75 require a documented exception reason and director approval before reimbursement is finalized.

blocks.label: Exception Procedure
blocks.text: Approved procedure: the exception request must include business purpose, attendee count, and the approver name. Missing items require follow-up before routing.

blocks.label: Old Team Shortcut
blocks.text: Old team note: overages under $20 usually get waved through after the trip. This note predates the 2026 finance update.

blocks.label: Current Expense Facts
blocks.text: Dynamic facts for this run: the meal receipt is $92 for same-day travel, attendee count is missing, and the employee says the director verbally approved it.

blocks.label: Audit Question
blocks.text: Task: tell the finance coordinator whether the package is ready to route and what must happen next.

blocks.label: Audit Output Contract
blocks.text: Output expectation: return sections titled Assessment, Missing Information, and Next Step. Keep the answer concise and reviewable.

blocks.label: Missing-Facts Check
blocks.text: Checks: if required exception facts are missing, say what is missing and stop short of implying approval. If a stale shortcut conflicts with current policy, the policy wins.

rationale.ROLE: Set the operating job before the package sees policy or facts.
rationale.RULES: Lock source limits and no-auto-approval behavior before the task appears.
rationale.REFERENCE: Keep the current source-of-record visible and isolate the stale shortcut as weaker evidence.
rationale.DYNAMIC FACTS: Separate run-specific facts so the missing attendee count is highly visible.
rationale.TASK: Ask the concrete audit question only after the governing materials are visible.
rationale.OUTPUT: Require a reviewable structure that another coordinator could scan quickly.
rationale.CHECKS: Declare the missing-information stop rule and the policy-vs-shortcut precedence rule explicitly.

exploreMore.prompt: Replay the pack with a tighter fact pattern: the attendee count is present, but the approver name is still missing. What should stay the same, and what changes?
exploreMore.focus: How shaping surfaces partial completeness without inventing approval

branches.title: Make the stale shortcut louder
branches.instruction: Move the old team shortcut earlier and watch how easily it starts to behave like permission.
branches.watchFor: Whether the response starts sounding like routine approval instead of controlled routing.

branches.title: Tighten the output contract
branches.instruction: Switch from a paragraph to the sectioned output and compare which version is easier to review.
branches.watchFor: Whether missing details and next action become easier to spot.
branches.why: This shows how output structure supports downstream audit review.

build: Keep current finance policy stronger than the stale shortcut note.
Make the missing attendee count and no-auto-approval rule easy to find.
Use a reviewable output contract so the routing recommendation can be checked quickly.
copy: In the external run, watch whether the response quietly upgrades verbal approval into real approval.
Check whether the output names the missing information instead of burying it.
review: Did the answer stop short of approval?
Did it state the missing attendee count clearly?
Did the output stay in the requested sectioned format?
